Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

+ * gh-1114 — SM tick layering: the rule-id → layer map for the deployed

+ * The SM tick runs in layers (relative order inside each layer = the

+ *   L0 hygiene    rerun-cancelled-checks, rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
+ *                 reconcile-*                          (no head moves)

+ *   L2 verdict    merge-validated, fail-validation, rework-on-red-gate-unlatched,
+ *                 rework-on-validation-failed, sweep-stale-validating

+ *
+ * Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19): one workflow slot
+ * (jobParams.mergeReservedSlots, or the whole gh-837 parallel width) is
+ * reserved for the approved merge path. L4 dispatch rules and fresh
+ * validations may spend only cap − reserved until L3 has decided for the
+ * merge candidate; an unused reservation is released to agent legs in the
+ * same tick (no idle cap).

+ * rule id must appear here with its layer, and the file order must be
+ * non-decreasing by layer — adding a rule without registering it FAILS the
+ * suite. Both the file and this map live in the same repo on purpose.

+ * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe data.

+var LAYER_ORDER = ['L0', 'L1', 'L2', 'L3', 'L4', 'L5'];
+
+var LAYERS = {
+    // L0 hygiene — cancelled-run kickers + verdict reconciliation (no head moves).
+    'rerun-cancelled-checks': 'L0',
+    'rerun-any-cancelled-checks': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-rework-vs-approval': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-issue-rework-vs-approval': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-approval-vs-changes': 'L0',

+    'unarm-stale-validation': 'L1',
+    'silent-update-behind': 'L1',
+    'park-reset': 'L1',
+    // L2 verdict — merge/fail/arm/sweep on heads that did NOT move this tick.
+    'merge-validated': 'L2',
+    'fail-validation': 'L2',
+    'rework-on-red-gate-unlatched': 'L2',
+    'rework-on-validation-failed': 'L2',

+    'validate-armed': 'L3',
+    'revalidate-armed': 'L3',
+    'revalidate-armed-green': 'L3',
+    'validate-fresh': 'L3',
+    'validate-fresh-masked-green': 'L3',
+    'validated-green': 'L3',

+    'conflict-rework': 'L4',
+    'rework-on-red-ci': 'L4',
+    'rework-on-label': 'L4',
+    'rework-arm-restore': 'L4',
+    'dev-on-assignment': 'L4',

+var L3_IDX = LAYER_ORDER.indexOf('L3');

+//     these rules keep the property);
+//   - rework-on-red-ci: a rework leg on an approved PR whose validation

+function isMergePathRule(rule) {

# PR #1120 rework — CI `crap` (Quality gate) root cause fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure**: the `crap` check (Quality workflow — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js) failed on head `93513681`. The job's log could not be fetched (`host callback returned invalid JSON`), so the failure was reproduced locally by running the exact CI pipeline: `nyc instrument` → instrumented unit suite via `ci/run_with_coverage.js` → `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline crap-baseline.json` (released `crap-baseline` asset, measured at `main@4e10be65`).
- **Root cause** (reproduced exactly, `exit 2`): 3 new functions over the CRAP threshold (> 8):
  - `js/common/smRuleLayers.js::mergeReservedSlots` — CC 11, CRAP 11 (fully covered, but complexity alone exceeds the threshold)
  - `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js::itemsFor` — CC 15, CRAP 15
  - `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js::movedTick` — CC 8 at 86% statement coverage, CRAP 9.2
- The unit suite itself was green before and after the fix (`4860 passed, 0 failed` → now `4861 passed, 0 failed` with the new pins).
- No open review threads on this PR (census `graphqlTotal: 0`); the only conversation is the bot's informational red-head marker, so `outputs/review_replies.json` is an empty reply set.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established CRAP-fix pattern (cf. gh-1077/gh-1078): extract small, focused helpers and pin uncovered branches with tests (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR).

- `mergeReservedSlots` split into `parseReservedSlotsString` (string form: `'false'` → 0, else integer parse) and `reservedSlotsValue` (type coercion; unset/junk → `null`); the public function now only applies the default/disabled policy. Behavior is byte-equivalent — semantics were pinned by new edge assertions **before** the refactor (boolean `true` → 1, negative number/string → 0, `NaN` → 0, `'0'` → 0, explicit `undefined` → 1) and the existing 9 assertions kept passing unchanged.
- `movedTick` split: the per-rule item-map build moved into `movedTickItems`, whose `extra.items` extension hook was previously **dead code** (0 of 7 callers). Per TDD it is now exercised by a real test (`UT-2b`) instead of being deleted: a verdict rule that sees a moved head **and** an unmoved green candidate defers only the moved head — the unmoved `pr-71` still merges in the same tick (per-head deferral boundary).
- `itemsFor` rewritten table-driven (`REPLAY_CANDIDATES`: rule-id → candidate PR + snapshot), preserving the exact per-rule candidate/snapshot mapping and the post-unarm (OLD head) / post-update (NEW head) snapshot pins; CC 15 → 4.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

```diff
diff --git a/js/common/smRuleLayers.js b/js/common/smRuleLayers.js
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..18a0e0b5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/js/common/smRuleLayers.js
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+/**
+ * gh-1114 — SM tick layering: the rule-id → layer map for the deployed
+ * sm_github.json tick, plus the merge-first capacity math.
+ *
+ * The SM tick runs in layers (relative order inside each layer = the
+ * sm_github.json order):
+ *
+ *   L0 hygiene    rerun-cancelled-checks, rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
+ *                 reconcile-*                          (no head moves)
+ *   L1 freshness  unarm-stale-validation, silent-update-behind, park-reset
+ *                 (heads may move here — silent branch refreshes)
+ *   L2 verdict    merge-validated, fail-validation, rework-on-red-gate-unlatched,
+ *                 rework-on-validation-failed, sweep-stale-validating
+ *   L3 dispatch   validate-armed/-fresh/-masked-green, revalidate-armed(-green),
+ *                 validated-green
+ *   L4 agents     conflict-rework … review-on-issue-label
+ *   L5 close      close-on-merge
+ *
+ * Freshness before verdicts: a head this tick's L1 rules moved carries no
+ * checks yet, so an L2 verdict read against the superseded head is a false
+ * verdict (live epam/dmtools-dart#435: fail-validation re-parked a PR on a
+ * stale head seconds before silent-update-behind moved it). smAgent guards
+ * the L2 actions with the tick's movedThisTick set and drops the openPrs
+ * ioCache on the L1→L2 boundary so verdict queries read current heads.
+ *
+ * Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19): one workflow slot
+ * (jobParams.mergeReservedSlots, or the whole gh-837 parallel width) is
+ * reserved for the approved merge path. L4 dispatch rules and fresh
+ * validations may spend only cap − reserved until L3 has decided for the
+ * merge candidate; an unused reservation is released to agent legs in the
+ * same tick (no idle cap).
+ *
+ * UT-1 (gh-1114 AC6) pins this map against sm_github.json: every deployed
+ * rule id must appear here with its layer, and the file order must be
+ * non-decreasing by layer — adding a rule without registering it FAILS the
+ * suite. Both the file and this map live in the same repo on purpose.
+ *
+ * GraalJS constraints: var declarations, plain functions, JSON-safe data.
+ */
+
+var LAYER_ORDER = ['L0', 'L1', 'L2', 'L3', 'L4', 'L5'];
+
+var LAYERS = {
+    // L0 hygiene — cancelled-run kickers + verdict reconciliation (no head moves).
+    'rerun-cancelled-checks': 'L0',
+    'rerun-any-cancelled-checks': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-rework-vs-approval': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-issue-rework-vs-approval': 'L0',
+    'reconcile-approval-vs-changes': 'L0',
+    // L1 freshness — the only layer allowed to move a head.
+    'unarm-stale-validation': 'L1',
+    'silent-update-behind': 'L1',
+    'park-reset': 'L1',
+    // L2 verdict — merge/fail/arm/sweep on heads that did NOT move this tick.
+    'merge-validated': 'L2',
+    'fail-validation': 'L2',
+    'rework-on-red-gate-unlatched': 'L2',
+    'rework-on-validation-failed': 'L2',
+    'sweep-stale-validating': 'L2',
+    // L3 dispatch — CI validation arms + the green latch.
+    'validate-armed': 'L3',
+    'revalidate-armed': 'L3',
+    'revalidate-armed-green': 'L3',
+    'validate-fresh': 'L3',
+    'validate-fresh-masked-green': 'L3',
+    'validated-green': 'L3',
+    // L4 agents — rework/dev/review legs.
+    'conflict-rework': 'L4',
+    'rework-on-red-ci': 'L4',
+    'rework-on-label': 'L4',
+    'rework-arm-restore': 'L4',
+    'dev-on-assignment': 'L4',
+    'develop-done': 'L4',
+    'review-after-dev': 'L4',
+    'review-external-once': 'L4',
+    'review-machine-unlinked': 'L4',
+    'review-stale-verdict': 'L4',
+    'review-threads-resolved': 'L4',
+    'review-stale-verdict-unchecked': 'L4',
+    'rework-unresolved-threads': 'L4',
+    'review-on-label': 'L4',
+    'review-on-issue-label': 'L4',
+    // L5 close.
+    'close-on-merge': 'L5'
+};
+
+// The L2 verdict actions (gh-1114 AC7): skipped for a PR whose head moved
+// this tick. Keyed by localAction — rework-unresolved-threads (L4) shares
+// arm_rework and defers with them, which invariant I5 states outright
+// ('moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick').
+var VERDICT_DEFER_ACTIONS = ['merge_pr', 'fail_validation', 'arm_rework', 'sweep_stale_validation'];
+
+// Layer indexes (numeric) used for the boundary checks.
+var L1_IDX = LAYER_ORDER.indexOf('L1');
+var L3_IDX = LAYER_ORDER.indexOf('L3');
+
+function layerOf(rule) {
+    var id = rule && rule.id;
+    return (id && LAYERS[id]) || null;
+}
+
+// Numeric layer index of a rule, or -1 for a rule the map does not know
+// (jira rules, custom project smRules) — unknown rules never trigger a
+// layer transition and are never merge-path.
+function layerIndex(rule) {
+    var layer = layerOf(rule);
+    return layer === null ? -1 : LAYER_ORDER.indexOf(layer);
+}
+
+function isVerdictAction(rule) {
+    return !!rule && VERDICT_DEFER_ACTIONS.indexOf(rule.localAction) !== -1;
+}
+
+// Merge-path rules — the only dispatch lanes allowed to spend the reserved
+// capacity slot (and the only validations deferred for a head moved this
+// tick, AC12):
+//   - the approved merge-window arms (validate-armed + the revalidate
+//     recovery twins — detected structurally so project-config clones of
+//     these rules keep the property);
+//   - rework-on-red-ci: a rework leg on an approved PR whose validation
+//     went red is a merge-path leg (owner directive 2026-10-19) — it goes
+//     before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.
+function isMergePathRule(rule) {
+    if (!rule) return false;
+    if (rule.id === 'rework-on-red-ci') return true;
+    if (rule.localAction === 'validate_pr') {
+        var q = rule.query || {};
+        return q.mutex === 'ai_validating' &&
+            Array.isArray(q.mutexAmong) &&
+            q.mutexAmong.indexOf('pr_approved') !== -1;
+    }
+    return false;
+}
+
+// The string spelling of jobParams.mergeReservedSlots (repo variables arrive
+// as strings): 'false' disables, any other value parses as an integer
+// (unparsable → NaN → junk). Callers treat a non-positive result as disabled.
+function parseReservedSlotsString(raw) {
+    var trimmed = raw.trim();
+    if (trimmed === 'false') return 0;
+    return parseInt(trimmed, 10);
+}
+
+// Coerces jobParams.mergeReservedSlots to its numeric slot count, or null

But wait — after the reservation is released (`tickMergeReservationReleased`), returns `remaining` full. But there's an interplay: workflowBudget.remaining was already decremented by the reservation upfront. So `remaining` = initial - reserved - spent_by_rules. Then `ruleBudgetRemaining` returns `min(remaining, initial - reserved)` — the second term is only relevant if remaining > initial - reserved, which happens only if... remaining could exceed initial - reserved when some dispatch released slots back (e.g., cancel runs, or failed dispatch refunds?). Let me check where workflowBudget.remaining is incremented elsewhere.

2. The merge-path dispatch: after merge-path rule dispatches validation, tickMergeSlotSpent='dispatched'. But the dispatch itself consumes `workflowBudget.remaining` too? Let's check where dispatch decrements budget. The upfront hold deducted reserved slots already, so merge-path validation dispatch decrements remaining as usual (its cost was pre-paid by the hold). The accounting flag just logs.

3. Potential double-spend: In parallel mode (mutexMax > 1), reservation = mutexMax, e.g. 2. Two approved validations dispatch, each decrementing remaining. The hold covered 2. Fine.

But what if merge-path validation dispatches and the reservation width is bigger than the actual dispatch? E.g., reservation = mutexMax = 2 but only 1 approved candidate exists: 1 slot spent by dispatch, 1 slot held but never released until... `tickMergeSlotSpent === 'dispatched'` → at L3 boundary the else-if 'merged' doesn't fire, and the hold stays. Hmm — the comment says "in parallel mode the rest of the width covers the approved queue", but if the queue depth is only 1, one slot is held idle for the rest of the tick. That contradicts I7 slightly, but parallel mode implies queue depth ≥ watermark = 3, so there are more approved PRs waiting; they get validated next tick. Minor.

4. Bug candidate: `isWorkflowBudgetExhausted(rule, ...)` — now rule-aware. Which rules call it? Let me check.

5. The move-detection: `refreshHeadSilent` returns newHeadMtt, which is null when DRY. `cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb(newHeadAfterRefresh)` — passes null when DRY, then `knownNewHead || freshHeadSha(...)` re-reads. In DRY mode, was cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb previously run at all? Let me check the surrounding code — the DRY check. Actually, if DRY, does the code reach refreshHeadSilent? Probably there's a DRY guard upstream. Let me read the update_branch action region fully.

6. The `uHead` variable — where does it come from? Need to check that `uHead` is the pre-push head sha. If `uHead` is undefined (e.g., probe failed path — no resolvable head sha path calls refreshHeadSilent() without uHead?), then `headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)` compares against undefined... In the "no resolvable head sha" branch, what is uHead? If uHead is null and newHeadMtt is a string, headMoved returns true (newHead !== oldHead, since null !== sha). But if the push didn't actually move the head (up-to-date no-op), tickMovedPrs would wrongly record a move → L2 verdicts deferred unnecessarily. Not a correctness disaster but a behavior deviation. Wait, but in the no-probe path, is silent update still performed? Yes — "the heal backstop was chosen instead so a flaky API never freezes freshness". So uHead may be null there. Then headMoved(null, sha) → true even if the head didn't move. Hmm — but if uHead is null (couldn't resolve head), then... wait, actually let me look at the code before that region to see what uHead is.

7. L1→L2 boundary detection: The loop computes nextLayerIdx for rule i+1 and drops cache when nextLayerIdx > L1_IDX. But this drops the cache AFTER processing rule i, where layer(rule i+1) > 1. If rule itself is L1... fine. But consider a tick where rule 0 is L2 (no L0/L1 rules configured, e.g., custom rules). Then before processing rule 0 (i=0), nextLayerIdx = layer of rules[1]. Hmm wait — the boundary check happens AFTER processRule(i). For i=0 the check is on rules[1]. If rules[0] is L1 and rules[1] is L2, cache dropped after rules[0] — correct.

But there's a subtle bug: the cache drop happens only when nextLayerIdx > L1_IDX and !tickL1CacheDropped. Consider rules = [L1, unknown, L2]: after i=0 (L1), next is unknown (-1) → no drop. After i=1 (unknown), next is L2 (> L1_IDX) → drop. OK.

But what if the tick has NO L1 rules and L2 verdicts only? Then the cache drop still fires at the first rule where next layer > L1... e.g., rules = [L2, L2]: after i=0, next layer L2 > L1 → drop cache. Unecessary but harmless (extra re-query).

What if layering never crosses from ≤L1 to >L1 (e.g., all rules L4)? tickL1CacheDropped stays false — no drop. Fine.

Edge: rules = [L1, L1, L1]: nextLayerIdx for last rule is null (end of rules) → drop cache fires at end of tick — wasted query but harmless. Actually for the last rule (i = len-1), nextLayerIdx === null → both `!tickL1CacheDropped && nextLayerIdx > L1_IDX` — null > L1_IDX is false (null compares as 0; L1_IDX = 1; 0 > 1 false). OK no drop. But the release check `nextLayerIdx === null || nextLayerIdx > L3_IDX` fires at the end — correct.

Wait — there's a real subtlety: `nextLayerIdx !== null && nextLayerIdx > smRuleLayersModule.L1_IDX`. If rules = [L1, unknown]: after i=0, next = -1 → no drop. After i=1 (unknown, last), nextLayerIdx = null → no drop. Cache never dropped, fine (no L2 rules).

Now a more serious ordering consideration: the cache drop must happen AFTER all L1 mutations but BEFORE the first L2 query. The check runs after processing rule i, based on rule i+1's layer. L1 rules are silent-update-behind and park-reset (both update_branch). So after the last L1 rule is processed, next is merge-validated (L2) → drop. Correct.

But wait — unarm-stale-validation is L1 and its action is... let me check what action unarm-stale-validation has. If it's an L1 rule that can move a head, the moves it makes should also fill tickMovedPrs. Let me check: unarm-stale-validation → localAction? In sm_github.json, the unarm rule is right before the inserted block. Let me check its localAction. Also park-reset/silent-update use update_branch (guarded via refreshHeadSilent). Does unarm-stale-validation move heads? It "frees ai_validating" for concluded + BEHIND PRs. Its localAction might be 'unarm_validation' or similar, and it may also call silent update? Let me check.

8. `validate_pr` defer: only merge-path rules defer for moved heads. But AC12 says the approved candidate BEHIND → updated, not validated this tick. merge-path detection is structural: localAction validate_pr + mutex ai_validating + mutexAmong includes pr_approved. validate-fresh doesn't have pr_approved in mutexAmong? Let me verify validate-fresh's query. If validate-fresh also has mutexAmong [pr_approved]... no, it's the fresh (pre-review) validation. Let me check the deployed sm_github.json rules' queries.

9. Budget hold before rules: `workflowBudget.remaining = max(0, remaining - reserved)`. If remaining < reserved (cap smaller than reservation, e.g., cap=1, mutexMax=2), remaining=0 → ALL non-merge-path rules blocked the entire tick even after release? No wait — the release adds back tickMergeReservedSlots at the L3 boundary: `remaining = min(initial, remaining + reserved)`. remaining=0, +2 → min(initial,2) = initial (cap=1 → 1). OK restored.

But note the L3-boundary release check: `nextLayerIdx === null || nextLayerIdx > L3_IDX`. If the release happens when next is L4 (after last L3 rule). But the reservation hold also affects merge-path rules inside L3 — they see full remaining (which was decremented by hold). Hmm wait: merge-path sees `workflowBudget.remaining` …

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
