Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1332
- **Deletions**: -50
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T22:28:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# gh-1114: SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)

## Description

## Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

## References
- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682,…

There was `if (!rule.localTeammate && workflowBudget) workflowBudget.remaining -= 1;` only at 5089 for triggered. For localAction paths — search for isWorkflowBudgetExhausted calls.

So my cap-starvation trace was wrong: localAction rules bypass the top-level budget gate entirely. The hold affects only non-localAction rules (agent legs, rerun rules?). Let me recheck the earlier cap=1 case: validate-armed (localAction) → budgetCapped false → no gate → dispatches. Agent legs (non-local): effBudget = min(remaining=0, ...) = 0 → skipped. So cap=1: merge path fine; agents starved until... the release at L3 boundary restores remaining=min(3?no, initial=1, 0+1)=1 → agent legs after L3 see remaining=1 → they dispatch. OK!

So the accounting actually works BECAUSE validate_pr rules don't decrement and aren't gated — the reservation hold only ever throttles agent lanes, and the L3-boundary release hands the hold back when unspent. Let me redo the UT-6 trace: cap 3, hold 1 → remaining 2. validate-armed dispatches (no decrement — validate_pr). Reviews (non-local): released at L3→L4 boundary? spent='dispatched' → NO release. Reviews see min(remaining=2, initial-reserved=2)=2 → 2 reviews → each decrements → remaining 0. Total = 3 dispatches. UT-6 passes.

Reviews: min(1, 3-2=1) = 1 → 1 review. Total = 2 validations... wait ciDispatches=1 (only one candidate), reviews=1 → total dispatches 2, cap 3, one unit held forever (spent='dispatched' → no release). The test asserts exactly this: 'cap 3 − reserved width 2 = 1 review slot (the width covers the approved queue while a validation is in flight)'. Hmm — so with concurrency=2, the tick wastes one unit: 2 real dispatches under cap 3. The second parallel arm — only one candidate existed in the test. In a real queue of ≥3 approved (watermark), validate-armed's limit is 2 → both arms dispatch (no decrement, budget gate bypassed for localAction) → 2 validations + min(remaining=1,1)=1 review = 3 = cap. OK that works.

Now the concurrency=3, cap=3 case: hold = 3 → remaining = 0. validate-armed limit patched to 3; localAction → budgetCapped=false → no gates → 3 arms dispatch! Reviews: remaining still 0 (validations don't decrement) → effBudget = min(0, ...) = 0 → reviews skipped... but wait, spent='dispatched' → release doesn't fire → reviews get 0. Total = 3 validations = cap 3. That's actually FINE — merge-first: the whole cap goes to approved validations. Reviews resume next tick. Hmm, so no starvation. Actually wait — does the hold of 3 with 3 arms dispatching = exactly cap? Yes: 3 validations dispatched, 0 reviews. Correct merge-first behavior (approved PRs outrun reviews).

What about validate-fresh (also validate_pr, non-merge-path, L3, BEFORE the L3→L4 boundary release)? validate-fresh runs AFTER validate-armed within L3. The reservation is still held (released only when nextLayer > L3_IDX after the LAST L3 rule). validate-fresh is localAction → not gated by budget → dispatches regardless. So fresh validations ignore the reservation entirely — they're "budget-free" like all validate_pr rules. The ticket says "L4 rules and validate-fresh can spend only cap − reservedForMerge" — but validate-fresh was never budget-gated (pre-existing: localAction rules bypass budget gates). So that part of the spec is vacuous. Fine — no regression.

Wait, but then what does the hold actually do at all? Only throttling agent (non-localAction) lanes: effBudget = min(remaining, initial - reserved) while held. remaining is only decremented by agent dispatches (and ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount). Hold: remaining = initial - reserved - active. min(x, initial-reserved) = remaining. So the effective cap for agents while held = initial - reserved - active. Release at L3→L4 boundary when unspent/merged: remaining += reserved (back to initial - active...). When spent ('dispatched'): no release → agents' cap stays initial - reserved - active. So the reservation costs agent lanes one unit for the rest of the tick whenever a merge-path validation dispatched. That matches the intent: the reserved unit is "spent" on the approved validation. And since validate_pr dispatches don't decrement remaining, the held unit IS the validation's slot. Clever. OK.

While held, remaining ≤ initial-reserved always? remaining = initial - reserved - active ≤ initial - reserved. Yes (active ≥ 0). So both branches equal while held. After release: remaining = initial - active(+refunds); non-merge: min(remaining, initial-reserved) — here the min BINDS and wrongfully caps agents at initial - reserved even after the reservation was RELEASED and returned via `remaining += reserved`! ```js
function ruleBudgetRemaining(rule, workflowBudget) {
   if (!workflowBudget) return 0;
   if (smRuleLayersModule.isMergePathRule(rule)) return workflowBudget.remaining;
   if (tickMergeReservationReleased || tickMergeReservedSlots <= 0) {

Now, what about moves caused by OTHER sources within the tick? E.g., conflict-rework / rework legs dispatch async (don't move heads synchronously). close-on-merge (L5). reconcile rules (L0) — do they move heads? "no head moves" per the map comment. OK.

Now the DRY + cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb interplay: refreshHeadSilent in DRY returns null (no read). Wait: `if (!DRY) { newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(...) }` → in DRY, newHeadMtt stays null → returns null → `cancelStaleAfterRefreshUb(null)` → `knownNewHead || freshHeadSha(...)` → re-reads even in DRY? But park-reset matches NON-BEHIND parked PRs too — "The silent branch refresh inside the action is a no-op for a non-BEHIND head (git merge reports up-to-date, no push)".
